title: Control plane: rate-limit scaling policy updates to prevent churn + emit warnings/audit events
author: Benji Okafor
description: Problem: During the predictive autoscaling pilot we saw a few Dedicated deployments get into “config churn” where Console (and a couple of customer scripts) would rapidly flip scaling policy fields (min/max, predictive mode, cooldowns). This amplifies oscillation in the autoscaler loop and produces noisy audit trails. We also had at least one pilot support escalation where repeated updates were masking the root cause (forecast staleness + max-bound saturation). This PR adds server-side throttling for scaling policy updates and emits explicit warnings/audit events when updates are rejected or de-duped. Approach: (1) Introduce a per-deployment token bucket on the UpdateScalingPolicy API (Capacity Policy Service). Default: 5 updates / 10 minutes / deployment, burst=2. (2) Add a per-account “global” safety bucket (50 updates / 10 minutes) to protect control plane resources during bulk automation mistakes. (3) When throttled: return HTTP 429 with Retry-After, include a stable error code (CAPACITY_POLICY_UPDATE_RATE_LIMITED) and a human-friendly message for Console. (4) Emit audit events for both successful updates and rejected updates (capacity_policy.update_throttled), including actor, request_id, deployment_id, and limit window parameters. (5) Emit a structured log + counter metric for SRE visibility. (6) Provide a bypass for internal admin tooling only (RBAC: role=platform_admin) to unblock incident response, still audited. Notes/semantics: - Rate limiting is applied after auth/RBAC checks but before validation/mutation. - “No-op” updates (request body equals current effective policy after normalization) are accepted but do not consume a token; they still emit a debug log (not an audit event) to avoid audit spam. - Limits are enforced consistently across regions using Redis-backed buckets; if Redis is unavailable we fail open (allow update) but emit an error log + metric (policy_update_rate_limit_backend_error) so we can detect degraded protection. Rollout: Guarded behind feature flag dedicated_scaling_policy_update_throttling (default off). Pilot accounts can be enabled via existing per-account flag plumbing. Follow-up: Console UX will handle 429 by showing a non-blocking banner with retry guidance and linking to the autoscaler troubleshooting runbook.
commits: capacity-policy: add rate limit middleware + error codes
capacity-policy: redis token bucket implementation + config defaults
audit: emit capacity_policy.update_throttled event w/ required fields
metrics: add counters + structured logs for throttling outcomes
tests: integration coverage for 429 + no-op update behavior
review_conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can you confirm where in the request pipeline the limiter runs? We should not leak any signal before auth/RBAC. Also please document fail-open vs fail-closed behavior if Redis is down.

Benji Okafor (author): Limiter now runs after auth + RBAC (see scaling_policy.ts). Added a short comment + metric + log for Redis failures; we fail open to avoid blocking legitimate config changes during an incident.

Jordan Lee (review): Default values: 5/10m feels ok, but we should ensure we don’t consume tokens for no-op updates (Console tends to resubmit on save). Also are you normalizing fields before comparing? (e.g., cooldown seconds defaulting).
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Added normalization before equality compare; no-op updates don’t consume tokens and return 200 with unchanged policy. Added tests for both cases.

Rafael Mendes (review): For SRE: please add a paging-safe metric name and include labels that won’t explode cardinality. We should avoid actor_id in metric labels. Also: do we have a way to bypass during incident response?

Benji Okafor (author): Metric is capacity_policy.update_rate_limited_total with labels {region, outcome, limiter_scope}. No actor labels. Added RBAC-gated bypass for platform_admin only; still audited.
Felix Schneider (review): Console needs stable error code + Retry-After. Please include request_id in response body so support can correlate easily.
Benji Okafor (author): Added CAPACITY_POLICY_UPDATE_RATE_LIMITED and Retry-After header. Response body now includes request_id (already generated by gateway) and limit window details.
Ethan Park (final): Looks good. Please add a short entry to internal runbook on interpreting 429s and where to see throttling metrics.
Benji Okafor (author): Added section under “Config churn / repeated updates” with metric name and audit event type. Thanks.
rollout_notes: Enable dedicated_scaling_policy_update_throttling for pilot accounts only. Monitor: capacity_policy.update_rate_limited_total (outcome=throttled), audit event volume for capacity_policy.update_throttled, and Redis error metric policy_update_rate_limit_backend_error. If we see legitimate automation blocked, adjust defaults via config without redeploy.
release_notes: Internal: Added server-side throttling on Dedicated scaling policy update endpoints to prevent rapid config churn; rejected updates return 429 w/ Retry-After and emit audit events for compliance/debugging.
